- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) and prices are rising, model often underestimates the spike; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent mean), leading to overshoot; apply smoothing or lagged mean reversion to dampen short-term volatility.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias correction proportional to sentiment magnitude.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate the final 5–7 days; add a small upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to the latter half of the forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.17), model often exhibits mean-reversion bias; align forecast toward recent 7–14 day average rather than 30-day trend.
